To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have solved the crystal structure of the full-length PKA RIβ2:C1 holoenzyme and that this isoform is enriched in mitochondria.

the RIβ isoform of PKA is localized selectively in mitochondria, where its quaternary structure is different from the other isoforms, and that this localization and structure are likely to have biological importance.

the PKA RIα, RIβ, RIIα and RIIβ holoenzymes have different shapes and that the PKA hIoloenzymes have discrete subcellular localizations that are consistent with the unique biological roles of the different isoforms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the regulatory subunit of PKA in the regulation of the activity of PKA and the localization of PKA signaling in cells.
how signaling molecules, in particular, cAMP-dependent protein kinases, interact with their substrates and how these interactions are regulated by the environment.
the structure and function of the cAMP-dependent protein kinases (PKAs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PKA holoenzymes with RIβ subunits are distinct from those with RIα subunits in terms of quaternary structure.
the RIβ holoenzymes have a distinct quaternary structure, which has a significant impact on their biological functions.
RIβ is the only isoform to localize in mitochondria, and the structure of the RIβ2:C1 complex is different from that of RIα2:C1, RIβ2:Cα, and RIβ2:Cβ complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined the structure of the full length RIβ2:C1 holoenzyme complex, which allowed us to visualize all domains of the PKAR2:C2 complex, and showed how isoform-specific assemblies can create distinct quatemary structures even though individual R:C heterodimers are highly homologous.
the PKA RIα, RIβ, RIIα and RIIβ holoenzymes have distinct subcellular distributions, quaternary structures and biological roles, which are all important for cAMP signaling specificity.
the quaternary structure is the most important determinant of PKA isoform-specificity and that the RIβ isoform is the least studied and most important isoform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quaternary structure is a key determinant in the biological function of a protein complex.
the RIβ holoenzymes are unique and that their unique structure may be important for their biological functions.
PKA isoforms are not just redundant but that they are differentially localized and have unique quaternary structures that may allow them to perform distinct biological functions.
